'''Bjørn Håvard Wiik''' (born 17 February 1937 in [[Bruvik Municipality|Bruvik]], [[Norway]]; died 26 February 1999 in [[Appel, Germany]]) was a Norwegian [[elementary particle]] physicist, notable for his role in the experiment that produced the first experimental evidence for [[gluon]]s and for his influential role on later accelerator projects.<ref name="Wagner1999">{{cite journal|last1=Wagner|first1=Albrecht| title=Bjørn Wiik|journal=Physics Today|volume=52|issue=7|year=1999|pages=69–70|issn=0031-9228|doi=10.1063/1.2802806|bibcode = 1999PhT....52g..69W |doi-access=free}}</ref> Wiik was director of [[DESY]], in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]], from 1993 until his death.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=DESY director, Bjorn Wiik, dies |url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/1999/feb/26/desy-director-bjorn-wiik-dies |work=Physics World|date=February 26, 1999 |access-date=August 31, 2017 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Bjørn Wiik was born in [[Bruvik Municipality|Bruvik]] on 17 February 1937. During [[World War II]] he was evacuated to [[England]] via a British submarine, due to his father being a leader of the [[Norwegian resistance movement]]. He attended high school in [[Bergen]] and moved to Germany to study physics at the [[Technical University of Darmstadt|Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref name=ind1>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=C. H. Llewellyn |title=Obituary: Bjorn Wiik |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/obituary-bjorn-wiik-1080763.html |website=The Independent |access-date=19 October 2023 |date=15 March 1999}}</ref> In 1965, he got his doctorate degree there. Two years later he began working at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]] in [[Menlo Park, California]]. In 1972, Wiik returned to Germany, to the German Electron Synchrotron ([[DESY]]) in [[Hamburg]] where,  four years later, he was appointed lead scientist.

In 1978, Wiik and his collaborators began using DESY's newly commissioned PETRA electron–positron storage ring to look for hard-gluon [[bremsstrahlung]] events that would provide experimental support for the existence and role of gluons in mediating  [[strong interactions]] among [[quarks]].  Wiik and his team  soon observed and reported a type of event never described before: three particle-jets whose momenta lay in a plane. These results, widely believed to represent the after-effects of two quarks plus a gluon, were soon confirmed by many other groups. In 1995, the [[European Physical Society]] awarded its Prize for High Energy and Particle Physics to four physicists representing the [[TASSO collaboration]] ([[Paul Söding]], Bjørn Wiik, [[Günter Wolf]], and [[Sau Lan Wu]]) for demonstrating the existence of the gluon.<ref>"[http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29201 Twenty-five years of gluons] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006233054/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29201 |date=2011-10-06 }}", ''CERN Courier'', November 12, 2004. Retrieved on 2008-05-28.</ref>

Already during his stay at SLAC, Wiik had proposed a new type of particle accelerator, which would be based on colliding a beam of [[protons]] with a beam of [[electrons]].  In 1980, this idea took concrete form with the creation at DESY of the [[Hadron Elektron Ring Anlage|hadron-electron ring facility HERA]]). Wiik was also responsible for proposing and overseeing the implementation of a superconducting linear accelerator for Tera-electronvolt energies, TESLA.<ref name=desy1>{{cite press release|title=DESY mourns for Prof. Dr. Bjørn H. Wiik |publisher=[[DESY]] |date=February 27, 1999 |url=http://www.desy.de/e428/e548/e4802/e4919/e4925/index_eng.html|accessdate=2017-08-31 }}</ref>

Wiik was chairman of the [[Super Proton Synchrotron]] Experiments Committee (SPSC) at [[CERN]] from 1979 to 1980<ref>{{cite web |url=http://library.cern/archives/history_CERN/Scientific_committees#SPSC1 |title=Super Proton Synchrotron Committee (SPSC) - 1st Period, 1973 – 1990 |publisher= CERN Archives |access-date=August 31, 2017}}</ref> and of the International Committee for Future Accelerators, a working group of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]], from 1997 to 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Membership {{!}} ICFA |url=https://icfa.hep.net/membership/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 1989 ''"for his contributions to the realization of the large electron-proton colliding beam facility, HERA, at the Deutsches Electron Synschotron Laboratory in Hamburg, West Germany"'' <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1989&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate= 5 October 2020}}</ref>

In 1995 he was awarded the [[High Energy and Particle Physics Prize|High Energy Particle Physics Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]], together with [[Paul Söding|Paul Soding]], Gunter Wolf, [[Sau Lan Wu]], "for the first evidence for three-jet events in e+e- collisions at PETRA".<ref>{{Cite web |last=High Energy Particle Physics Division of EPS |title=The High Energy Particle Physics Prizes |url=https://eps-hepp.web.cern.ch/hepp-prize-awards.php |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=eps-hepp.web.cern.ch}}</ref>

Wiik died on 26 February 1999 in Appel at the age of 62 due to "an accident at home".<ref name=ind1/><ref name=desy1/>
